learning_outcomes.text: Ability to design and develop applications, ensuring their reliability, security, and quality, in accordance with ethical principles and current legislation and regulations.
Ability to select and evaluate computer systems, ensuring their reliability, security, and quality, in accordance with ethical principles and current legislation and regulations.
Knowledge of computer systems, services, and applications.
Knowledge, design, and efficient use of the most appropriate data types and structures for problem solving.
Knowledge of the characteristics, functionalities, and structure of Operating Systems.
Design and implement applications based on Operating System services.
Knowledge and application of the fundamental principles and basic techniques of parallel and concurrent programming.
Understand the different types of operating systems, along with their characteristics and capabilities, that can be used as system software in the design and development of a computer system.
Be able to select and evaluate the most appropriate type of operating system to provide a service ensuring the required quality characteristics.
Knowledge of the components and applications that integrate an operating system distribution.
Understand how data structures are used in managing the components and functions of an operating system.
Know the structure of an operating system.
Understand the basic operating mechanisms of the subsystems that integrate an operating system.
Design and implement applications based on the services of an operating system.
Understand the use of basic parallel and concurrent programming techniques in the operating mechanisms of operating systems.

syllabus_topics: Programming with system calls in UNIX. Implementation of a command interpreter
assessment_rules: For ordinary assessment, a minimum score of 4.5 out of 10 is required for both the theoretical and practical blocks. The theoretical block grade is (0.5 * T1) + (0.5 * T2). The practical block grade is (0.4 * P1) + (0.1 * PA1) + (0.4 * P2) + (0.1 * PA2), provided attendance requirements are met; otherwise, scores for P1/PA1 or P2/PA2 may be zeroed. The final grade is (0.65 * Theory) + (0.35 * Practical) if minimums are met, otherwise it's the minimum of the calculated score and 4.0. For the extraordinary assessment, a theoretical exam and a practical exam cover all content, with a minimum of 4.5 in each, and the final grade is calculated using the same 0.65/0.35 weighting.
